answer.evidence: The rack is drawn flat-on as a front elevation. The crossbeam (rows 5-9) is a front-facing strip with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The posts are vertical strips. The six sheaves (rows 3-26) are vertical shapes with dome-like rounded tops and a bright yellow grain band at rows 21-25. No row shows a horizontal surface seen from above: there is no ellipse, no roof or canopy plane and no visible contents of an open container. There is no receding side face. The silhouette widths hold at 45-48 across rows 5-24, so there is no top plane that widens and narrows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small drying-rack prop (wooden poles with hanging rice bundles), not a whole building with roof, walls and door, so the building references are not a like-for-like comparison. The measured facts do not count against it: 20 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, which means the outlines are tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, though, the rack is thin and sparse. The wood poles show about 3 steps and the rice bundles about 3-4 flat-ish yellow/ochre steps. It lacks the per-tile highlights, grain and clump texture the references carry on their roof and wall surfaces. Placed next to the references it reads as thinner and simpler, with little per-bundle texture. With the kind mismatch and the shallower shading, I fail it under the 'when in doubt, fail' rule.

surfaces.part: rice bundles (six hanging sheaves, rounded tops)

answer.evidence: The main body is a row of six hanging rice bundles seen face-on. Each bundle has a narrow rounded head at rows 3-6, a darker tie band at rows 12-13, and a vertical body down to a yellow butt end at rows 21-25. The head is a rounded hat, not an ellipse with a front rim. The crossbeam at rows 5-9 is a thin front-facing strip, and the only hint of an edge is a dark row 9, so at most 1-2 rows read as a top. No horizontal surface, roof or ellipse is visible on the bundles, and the posts are drawn as plain vertical faces. The width profile only widens to 48 and stays level, so there is no top-surface band. The drawing is a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are whole buildings (tiled roof, plaster or stone walls, door), but the candidate is a small open rice-drying rack: wooden poles with hanging golden bundles. The kinds do not match, so the comparison is only approximate. The measured facts favour the candidate: 20 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and dark-brown beside the wood. By eye, though, it is thin and sparse. The poles are mostly 2-3 brown tones with little grain. Each bundle has only about 3 yellow-orange steps and a few dark dots. It lacks the 5-6 step ramps and per-element texture, such as per-tile highlights and stone-by-stone shading, that the references show. It would look slightly thinner and flatter than the references. The wrong reference kind and the sparse look together mean it fails.
